title: Response playbook: voice-call prep & follow-up (scratch)
content:
Purpose:
- Quick single-sheet prep for an ad-hoc voice call with a paying customer (Acme Analytics) experiencing model-serving latency spikes during batch scoring. Keep this focused: get to containment, assign owners, and confirm next steps.

Call objective (15–25 min):
- Verify customer impact and SLAs affected (latency > 2s p95 on /v1/generate for batch-run).
- Confirm containment steps we can run during the call (fallback model, throttling, disable heavy reranking).
- Assign immediate owners and timeboxed actions.
- Agree on communication cadence and internal follow-up.

Pre-call quick checks (5 min, do these before dialing in):
- Ticket: CS-4873 – read last customer message.
- Logs: tail last 200 lines from model-serving pod (kubectl -n redwood logs -f deploy/model-serve --tail=200).
- Metrics: open Grafana panel - model-serving latency (p50/p95/p99), queue depth, GPU utilization for the last 30m.
- Recent deploys: check last rolling deploy (git tag + CI pipeline ID) and note if any model or infra change in last 2 hrs.
- Known mitigations: fallback to quantized-variant v1-q, enable prefix-cache (if safe), or increase autoscale target for dedicated pool.

Attendees / suggested roles (modify as needed):
- Jasper Reed (you) — call lead / notes / customer comms.
- Maya Patel — runtime engineer (attempts live mitigation).
- Rowan Li — SRE (infrastructure-level throttle / scale).
- CS AE (Acme contact) — customer readout.
- Optional: Eng on-call for model (if deploy-level rollback likely).

Suggested call agenda (time-boxed):
1) 0:00–02:00 Introductions / objective (Jasper)
2) 02:00–06:00 Customer describes observed behaviour & business impact (AE)
3) 06:00–12:00 Rapid diagnostics review (Maya/Rowan) — metrics, recent deploys, errors
4) 12:00–18:00 Containment proposal & quick actions (choose 1 or 2):
   - Switch route to fallback model variant (v1-q quantized) — expected cost/latency tradeoffs
   - Apply request-level throttling (limit concurrency per API key) for batch jobs
   - Temporarily disable heavy reranking step in pipeline
5) 18:00–22:00 Assign owners / ETA on actions (who will execute and check-in times)
6) 22:00–25:00 Customer comms & wrap-up: next update time, escalation path

Live troubleshooting checklist (ordered, practical commands):
- Confirm impact windows on Grafana -> note timestamps for scope.
- kubectl -n infra get hpa, pods, nodes -> check scaling issues.
- kubectl -n redwood exec -it svc/model-proxy -- curl -s -D - -o /dev/null "http://localhost:8080/health"
- tail logs for error patterns: connection resets, OOMs, long GC pauses.
- If model variant rollback chosen: route-switch command (internal): rtr switch --route acme-prod --model v1-q --confirm
- If throttling chosen: apply policy via console -> RateLimit: key=acme-prod, concurrency=2, burst=4

Containment decision guide (quick heuristics):
- If p95 latency > 2s and GPU utilization < 60% -> likely model-level compute inefficiency or hot KV cache misses: try quantized fallback or restart serving workers.
- If queue depth spikes and autoscaler not reacting -> scale config / HPA issue: escalate to SRE; temporarily throttle incoming requests.
- If recent commit touched tokenizer or attention fusion -> rollback to previous release and test on canary.

Customer message templates (copy-paste and adapt)
- Opening (0–2 min): "Thanks for taking this call. We see the latency spike you reported and our priority is containment while we investigate root cause. We will propose a short set of actions and agree an immediate plan. ETA for first corrective action: 15 minutes."
- After action applied: "We've switched you to a lower-latency fallback variant and are monitoring. We expect latency improvement; will confirm within 10 minutes and follow with a root-cause update."

Roles / RACI quick map (for this call):
- Responsible: Maya (runtime mitigation), Rowan (infra scaling), Jasper (external comms + notes)
- Accountable: CS AE (customer sign-off on mitigation), Jasper (ensuring follow-ups happen)
- Consulted: Eng on-call (deploy/rollback decisions)
- Informed: Product PM (if model variant changes affect feature behavior)

Immediate post-call actions (0–24h):
- Within 15m: confirm containment result + post to slack #cust-acme-ops (Jasper)
- Within 60m: collect logs, snapshots, and add to CS-4873 (Maya) -> attach Grafana snapshots and kubectl dumps (pods/nodes).
- Within 3h: if rollback executed, run regression smoke tests on canary and report results (Eng on-call)
- Within 6h: prepare short incident email to customer summarizing root cause hypothesis and next steps (Jasper + AE)
- By EOD: internal postmortem outline (template) created in Confluence with action owners (Rowan)

Longer-term follow-ups (48–72h):
- Confirm permanent config changes (autoscale tuning, model-variant defaults) and schedule a controlled deploy window (Product + Infra).
- Run load replay using synthetic batch from Acme traces in staging and report delta.
- Add a synthetic alert (p95 > 1.5s) to avoid regression.

Notes-to-self / heuristics learned (for future calls):
- Keep the call to 25 minutes max. Rapid containment then offline RCA works better for engineering productivity.
- Have the route-switch command pre-authorized for this customer in the console — saves precious minutes.
- Standardize the 3 containment options and keep the cost/latency tradeoffs documented in one slide.

Scratch log (live notes) -- fill during call: 
- 14:02: customer reports spike started 13:47, affected batch jobs only, interactive calls ok.
- 14:05: Grafana p95 = 3.7s, GPU util = 42%, queue depth = 120 (baseline 15).
- 14:08: last deploy 13:40 (model code + tokenizer) -> potential suspect.
- 14:12: applied throttling (concurrency->2) -> queue depth dropped to 40, p95 -> 2.1s.
- 14:18: switched to v1-q fallback -> p95 -> 1.0s; customer confirms improvement.

Post-call artifacts to attach to ticket CS-4873:
- Grafana snapshots (before/after), kubectl pod dumps, routing change command audit logs, timestamps of customer confirmations.

Open questions / things to validate after the call:
- Why did autoscaler not increase worker count? (HPA metrics, cloud provider throttles?)
- Is the tokenizer commit causally linked to latency? Run unit perf tests.
- Are there cache-warmup steps we can do on deploy to avoid cold-start penalties for large prefix loads?

Personal checklist before closing ticket:
- [ ] Draft and send customer follow-up email (template above).
- [ ] Add regression test to nightly suite covering this scenario.
- [ ] Confirm alert threshold changed and document in runbook.
- [ ] Schedule retrospective sync with PM/infra next week.

End-of-doc note: this is a lightweight, portable pad for phone/Zoom calls. Keep it short, copy the bits you need into a formal incident report after we have evidence.
